body.statement: In the one-donor equal-Bernoulli post subexperiment with donor knot displacement \(h_B/\sqrt{m_\ell}\), the simplex is the singleton \(\Delta_1=\{1\}\), so \(\widehat w_\ell=w_\ell=1\), \(v_\ell=0\), and the weight quadratic, \(B_{t,\ell}\) cross contribution, and all \(\epsilon_{t,\ell}\) remainder terms are identically zero.  The anchored limit is \(\Psi^B_{h_B}=|Z_0-h_B-Z_1|+|Z_0|+|Z_1|-|Z_0-h_B|-|h_B+Z_1|+h_B\), where \(Z_0,Z_1\) are independent \(N(0,1/4)\).  Its exact distribution function reduces to a one-dimensional Gaussian integral, and the least common \(95\) percent squared-radius cutoff \(c_B^*\) satisfies \(1.913<c_B^*\leq1.914\), while the collision-oracle cutoff is \(1.38590382435\) to the displayed decimal precision.  Any plug-in-centered squared radius whose balls have asymptotic coverage at least \(0.95\) uniformly over the local offsets and whose normalized radius has a deterministic collision limit \(c\) must satisfy \(c\geq c_B^*\).
body.proof_tex:
The corrected statement fixes the coverage level at \(0.95\).  With \(J=1\), the simplex is \(\Delta_1=\{1\}\), so the empirical minimization cannot change the weight: \(\widehat w_\ell=w_\ell=1\) and \(v_\ell=0\).  Every term containing \(v_\ell\), including the weight quadratic, the \(B_{t,\ell}\) term, and all three \(\epsilon_{t,\ell}\) remainder terms, is therefore identically zero.

Let the treated population knot be \(1/2\), the donor knot be
\(1/2+h_B/\sqrt{m_\ell}\), and let
\(Z_0,Z_1\) be the independent limits of their centered empirical knots.  The multinomial central limit theorem gives
\(Z_0,Z_1\sim N(0,1/4)\).  The four separately anchored pairs have coefficients and local endpoints
\[
 (-1,Z_0),\quad(1,0),\quad(1,h_B+Z_1),\quad(-1,h_B).
\]
Substitution into \(-\tfrac12\sum_{q,q'}b_qb_{q'}|s_q-s_{q'}|\) and collection of the six unordered pairs gives
\[
 \Psi^B_{h_B}=|Z_0-h_B-Z_1|+|Z_0|+|Z_1|-|Z_0-h_B|-|h_B+Z_1|+h_B.
\]

For completeness, put \(S=Z_1-Z_0\) and \(R=Z_1+Z_0\).  These variables are independent \(N(0,1/2)\).  If \(h_B+S\geq0\), direct comparison of the true interval with the empirical signed interval gives
\[
 \Psi^B_{h_B}=\max\{|S|,\min(|R|,2h_B+S)\}.
\]
If \(S=-A<-h_B\), reversing the empirical interval gives
\[
 \Psi^B_{h_B}=A+\min\{2\min(h_B,A-h_B),(A-|R|)_+\}.
\]
These identities follow by ordering the four endpoints in each case and summing the constant squared error on the intervening intervals; they also follow by expanding the preceding six-term formula.

Let \(P(x)=\Phi(\sqrt2x)\), \(G(x)=2P(x)-1\), and
\(f(x)=e^{-x^2}/\sqrt\pi\).  Conditioning on \(S\), using independence of \(R\), and splitting at the two displayed order changes yields, for \(q>0\),
\[
 F_h(q):=\Pr(\Psi^B_h\leq q)=G(q)^2,\qquad h\geq q,
\]
and, for \(0\leq h<q\),
\[
 a(h,q)=\max\{q-2h,(q+2h)/3\},
\]
\[
 F_h(q)=2P(q)^2-1+2\{1-P(q)\}P(q-2h)
 -\int_{a(h,q)}^q f(z)G(2z-q)\,dz. \tag{1}
\]
This is the claimed one-dimensional Gaussian integral.  When
\(0\leq h\leq q/4\), the lower endpoint is \(q-2h\), and differentiation under the integral gives
\[
 \frac{\partial F_h(q)}{\partial h}
 =-4\{1-P(q)\}f(q-2h)-2f(q-2h)G(q-4h)\leq0.
\]
When \(q/4\leq h<q\), the lower endpoint is \((q+2h)/3\) and
\[
 \frac{\partial F_h(q)}{\partial h}
 =-4\{1-P(q)\}f(q-2h)
 +\frac23f((q+2h)/3)G((4h-q)/3). \tag{2}
\]
For \(h\geq q\), the first formula shows that the CDF is constant.  Hence the global minimum for fixed \(q\) is found on \([q/4,q]\), together with its endpoints.

Here is a finite arithmetic certificate for the strict bracket.  For every
\(|x|\leq1.914\), enclose
\[
 \operatorname{erf}(x)=\frac{2}{\sqrt\pi}
 \sum_{k=0}^{43}\frac{(-1)^kx^{2k+1}}{k!(2k+1)}+\mathcal R_{43}(x),
\]
using
\[
 |\mathcal R_{43}(x)|\leq
 \frac{2}{\sqrt\pi}\frac{|x|^{89}}{44!\,89},\qquad
 0.5641895835477562<\pi^{-1/2}<0.5641895835477564.
\]
The remainder bound follows because the alternating terms decrease from index four onward.  Thus all evaluations below are rational interval operations.  Partition each integration interval in (1) into \(200000\) equal subintervals.  Since \(G(2z-q)\) is increasing,
\[
 \sum_kG(2z_k-q)\{P(z_{k+1})-P(z_k)\}
 \leq\int_a^qG(2z-q)dP(z)
 \leq\sum_kG(2z_{k+1}-q)\{P(z_{k+1})-P(z_k)\}.
\]
The displayed enclosure of \(\pi^{-1/2}\) is itself certified without floating-point assumptions: use Machin's identity
\[
 \pi=16\arctan(1/5)-4\arctan(1/239)
\]
and enclose both arctangents by the first \(30\) terms of their alternating rational power series.  The first omitted terms bound the two remainders; squaring the two stated decimal rationals and comparing their reciprocals with the resulting rational enclosure of \(\pi\) gives the asserted strict inequalities.
Partition \([q/4,q]\) into \(200000\) equal offset intervals.  From (2),
\[
 \left|\frac{\partial F_h(q)}{\partial h}\right|
 \leq\frac{4\{1-P(q)\}+2/3}{\sqrt\pi}<0.384
\]
for both rational values of \(q\) used below.  Applying the nearest-grid allowance, the series remainder, and a final outward-rounding allowance of \(10^{-8}\) gives the exact rational enclosures
\[
 F_{0.4929}(1.913)<0.949941881<0.95,
\]
and
\[
 \inf_{h\geq0}F_h(1.914)>0.950023317>0.95.
\]
The first inequality shows \(c_B^*>1.913\), and the second shows
\(c_B^*\leq1.914\).

At collision, \(h=0\) and \(\Psi^B_0=|Z_0-Z_1|\), where
\(Z_0-Z_1\sim N(0,1/2)\).  Its exact \(0.95\) quantile is therefore
\[
 q_0=\frac{\Phi^{-1}(0.975)}{\sqrt2},
\]
which is \(1.38590382435\) to the displayed decimal precision.

It remains to prove the honesty obstruction.  Under collision, the likelihood ratio for changing the donor mass from \(1/2\) to \(1/2+h/\sqrt{m_\ell}\) satisfies, with \(\widehat p\) the donor empirical mass,
\[
 \log L_{h,\ell}=4h\sqrt{m_\ell}(\widehat p-1/2)-2h^2+o_{P_0}(1)
 \Rightarrow N(-2h^2,4h^2).
\]
Moreover \(E_0L_{h,\ell}^2=(1+4h^2/m_\ell)^{m_\ell}\) is bounded, and the corresponding reverse likelihood ratios are bounded in \(L^2\) for large \(\ell\).  Cauchy--Schwarz therefore proves mutual contiguity directly.  If a plug-in-centered squared radius satisfies
\(\sqrt{m_\ell}R_\ell^2\to c\) in probability at collision, contiguity gives the same convergence under every fixed \(h\).  Joint loss convergence and continuity of (1) at positive \(c\) imply that uniform \(0.95\) coverage requires
\[
 \inf_{h\geq0}F_h(c)\geq0.95.
\]
By the definition of \(c_B^*\), this forces \(c\geq c_B^*\).  Since
\(c_B^*>1.913>q_0\), collision-oracle deterministic calibration is not uniformly honest.
